reset()

The reset() method clears the current state of a FeatureCell and returns it to a neutral, non-loading state without tearing down the FeatureCell or its runtime infrastructure.

Method Contract Summary

  • Clears the current state value
  • Clears any associated error state
  • Resets loading indicators
  • Does not destroy the FeatureCell
  • Allows continued pipeline execution

The reset() method defines state reset only. It does not unregister behaviors, destroy controllers, or terminate the FeatureCell lifecycle. After a reset, the FeatureCell remains fully initialized and operable.

Note

Unlike destroy(), calling reset() does not finalize the FeatureCell. The cell may continue to receive updates, execute pipelines, and emit new state snapshots after the reset completes.

Method Contract
Runtime Invocation
Method Description
reset()

inputs:

  • None

return:

  • void
 Clears the FeatureCell’s current state and error information while preserving its initialized runtime surface. The FeatureCell remains active and may continue processing updates.
State Shape After Reset

When reset() is called, the StateSnapshotShape.value is set to undefined. The FeatureCell remains initialized, but its committed state value is cleared.

Depending on the structural expectations of your FeatureCell, you may need to explicitly re-establish a valid state shape before continuing execution. This is especially important when merge behaviors or stream-based updates assume a specific value type (such as an array or object).

For example, if your FeatureCell relies on array-based merge semantics, you should restore the value to an empty array: 

{{ `this.vault.replaceState({value: []});` }}
 
{{ `employeeCell.replaceState({value: []});` }}

Reset clears state — it does not reconstruct your domain shape. If subsequent updates depend on a non-undefined structure, that structure must be restored explicitly.

Example

Calling reset() clears the FeatureCell’s current state and error information while keeping the FeatureCell active.

Example: Resetting a FeatureCell

{{`// Reset the FeatureCell state

this.vault.reset();

// FeatureCell remains initialized and operable`}}
 
{{`// Reset the FeatureCell state

employeeCell.reset();

// FeatureCell remains initialized and operable`}}

What this does

  • Clears the current state value
  • Clears any associated error
  • Emits a reset lifecycle event
  • Preserves all registered behaviors and controllers

After reset, subsequent updates are processed normally, and new state snapshots may be emitted as pipeline execution resumes.
